reflection.theme: The Ordinary Miracle of a Regular Thursday
reflection.quote: The most beautiful thing we can experience is the mysterious. It is the source of all true art and science.
reflection.reading:
Mid-August has a particular quality to it. The summer isn't over, but you can feel it starting to lean. Evenings come a few minutes earlier. The tomatoes are finally in. You've either done the summer things you wanted to do, or you haven't, and there's still a little time left to change that. It's a Thursday in the middle of a month that doesn't announce itself. Nothing about today is remarkable.

That used to be exactly the kind of day I couldn't handle. A Tuesday, a Thursday, a random Wednesday in February — days without occasion were the hardest to be sober through, because there was nothing to reach for and nothing to celebrate. Just the day itself, asking me to be in it. Drinking gave those days a shape. Sobriety asked me to find the shape without help.

What I've learned is that the ordinary days are the whole thing. Not the big trips, not the milestones, not the anniversaries. It's the drive home from work with the windows down. The coffee that tastes like coffee. The text from a friend you actually answer. A regular Thursday, met without needing to escape it, is a life. You don't have to make it profound. You just have to be here for it, and eventually you realize being here for it is the profound part.
reflection.meditation: What would it look like to meet today without needing it to be more than it is?

affirmations: I am building a life out of ordinary days, and that is enough.
Today I can be present without needing to escape or perform.
I have the capacity to show up for whatever this day asks of me.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a day that doesn't require anything spectacular of me. Grateful for a clear head on a Thursday morning, for work I can do, for people I actually recognize when they call. Grateful that the quiet days don't scare me the way they used to. Grateful to be here for another one.
gratitude.closing: One more ordinary day, met on purpose.
